newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end firm, but fall still possible.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end firm, but fall still possible.

text.p: Singapore's benchmark share measure, the Straits Times Industrials Index (STII), closed up on Thursday, against earlier market expectations, as several key index components surged in the last few minutes of trading.
But dealers said the unweighted 30-share index, which finished 19.81 points higher at 2,214.17, was likely to fall back again on Friday ahead of the weekend on profit-taking.
"The index jumped on the back of just a few stocks: Fraser & Neave, Cerebos and Sembawang," said one institutional dealer.
Chartists viewed the close as positive but said the index must end above 2,220 before its consolidation was complete.
The STII reached an intra-day high of 2,221.23 on November 26 but then slipped back to 2,177.79 on Wednesday, prompting predictions of a further fall to 2,150-2,125.
Many of Thursday's gainers were overseas stocks, including China Merchants, which rose 30 cents to HK$5.50, and Guangzhou Investments, which was up 15 cents to HK$3.10.

Top of the volume was computer training group Informatics which saw a total of 12 million shares crossed off the market at Singapore $0.64 in the last few minutes of trade. The share ended unchanged at S$0.62.
